svg.text: JOURNAL: how the log chain fills
The journal is restored and empty
lsn 1 (prev 0) is written: its pages go to log data, the record to log meta - it continues the chain, so it is indexed and
lsn 3 (prev 2) arrives before lsn 2: it is durable but pending, the user waits
lsn 2 (prev 1) fills the gap: lsn 2 and lsn 3 are indexed together
The user acks up to lsn 3: LsnLowWatermark = 3, these records may leave the journal
The flusher copies the pages of lsn 1 to the data store: LastFlushedLsn = 1
lsn 2 and lsn 3 are flushed too: LastFlushedLsn = 3
Cleanup erases the flushed records from log meta and frees their log data pages
lsn 6 (prev 5) arrives before lsn 5: pending - it reuses the freed pages
lsn 5 (prev 4) fills the gap: lsn 5 and lsn 6 are indexed
lsn 8 (prev 7) arrives: pending, waiting for lsn 7
lsn 9 (prev 6) continues from lsn 6, skipping lsn 7: lsn 8 can never join the chain, it is stranded. lsn 9 spans two log data
The user acks up to lsn 9: LsnLowWatermark = 9
Cleanup erases them - and the stranded lsn 8, whose user gets E_INVALID_STATE. The data store keeps what was flushed
